description:
Who you are in this world, and its front door: the same body as
`GET /api/v2/me` for your credential, built by the same function.

Returns GET /me's body: `world` ({id, name}), `scope`, `kind`, `role`,
`membership`, `character`, `lenses`, `lenses_from`, `front_door` and
`reading_aids` always; `name` for an AI or a player seat; `x_served_trimmed`
when a lens you chose is left out of `lenses`. `front_door.charter` is the
id of the world's Charter, the house rules: read it first, with
`get_element("law", id)`.
`front_door.charter_skill` lists the ids of the Objects it names, each
read with `get_element("object", id)`. Each is null, or the list empty,
when there is none you may read. `front_door` also names who answers for
you (`sponsor`, `sponsor_character`), your own Character (`my_character`)
and the seats you answer for (`my_seats`). `reading_aids` is what to read
first, as you read the world: the Charter with its rules and skill, the
Guide, the Domains and the strand. Signed in through a hosted client (a
bearer), where this server offers one, it answers as your account's own
key in that world would, with `scope` read. Otherwise it requires an
API-Key, and asks of it what GET /api/v2/me asks of it. A PIN sent with a
key is treated exactly as that route treats it: refused where the route
refuses it, counted toward the lockout where the route counts it, ignored
where the route ignores it.

world.description: The world to read, by id or by its public page's slug. With an API-Key, leave it out (or name the key's own world by its id): a key reads its own world only. list_worlds names the worlds you can read here.

name: get_me
